multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which component keeps data when the power is off?

div.p: RAM and cache are volatile — they lose their contents without power. Persistent data lives on storage such as an SSD or hard disk.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A desktop powers on, the fans spin, but there is no display and the motherboard emits a repeating beep pattern. The most useful first step is to:

choice.div: Look up the firmware beep code and reseat the indicated component.

div.p: POST beep codes point at a specific subsystem, most often memory or video. Decode the code, then reseat or swap that component before touching anything else.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Before opening a computer case, you should:

choice.div: Leave it running so you can watch the fans.
Power it down, unplug it, and discharge static from yourself.
Wear a grounded wrist strap while it is still plugged in.

div.p: Power down and disconnect first, then equalise your static charge by touching bare metal or using an anti-static strap. Never work inside a live machine.
